rhythm.value: Corrected: 13 shots, 12 boundaries (10 hard cuts, 2 circle wipes), median shot 2.0 s, 23.9 boundaries a minute, shortest 1.07 s, longest 5.63 s (end card). The detector read 19 shots, 18 boundaries, median 1.3 s, 35.8 a minute: 7 of its boundaries were text or rows added on a held layout, and it missed one real cut (13.233 s). Rule used: a boundary counts when the subject or the ground changes; an element added to a held layout (a word, a checklist row, a typed line) does not, whatever its score. That keeps 7.833 s (word replaced by the mark, sceneScore 0.04) and rejects 1.3, 10.033, 14.133, 14.533, 15.1, 19.833 and 22.5 s. The 21.1 s boundary is one frame early: the new headline first shows at F634 (21.133 s); times here keep 21.1. Shape: a 2.0 s hook, three 1.07-1.6 s shots for the name reveal (fastest stretch, 5.53-9.43 s), then longer demo and proof shots (1.7-3.6 s) and a 5.63 s end card. Inside shots the clock is the animation, not the cut: a new word every 10 frames in the hook, a letter every 2-3 frames in typed names, checklist rows at F424, F436, F453, F459. Sound: I cannot hear. Tempo 125.8 BPM at confidence 0.127 (beat regularity 0.94), so no beat grid is claimed. On the corrected cuts 5 of 12 land within 80 ms of a beat against 0.33 by chance (lift 1.27; 2 of 6 before 9.94 s and 3 of 6 after, the two loudness sections), 0 of 12 within a frame of a downbeat against 0.036, signed median cut-to-beat -0.023 s; onsets run 4.9 a second, so the onset ratio (7 of 12 against 0.71 by chance) says nothing; loudness swells (50 ms RMS, local maximum over 0.3 s each side, above 1.35x median, 29 found) meet 2 of 12 cuts against 0.16 by chance. No evidence that cuts follow the music. The detector's sync.json (18 cuts) says the same: 0.333 on beat against 0.313, onsets 0.667 against 0.692. No speech was transcribed (speech layer unavailable), and the screen carries all the words.

value.name: word-build-tinted-arrival
value.description: Promise line built on #FEFEFE, a new word about every 10 frames (F0, F9, F19, F29, F40). Each new word appears whole and enters pale lilac (#B873B3), turns raspberry (#B73A69) on the next frame, then teal (#0A7F6F), and settles to ink #030303 about 5 frames after it appeared (e.g. F9-F14). The line stays centred, so it shifts left as each word lands; at F39 the letter spacing tightens for a frame before the last word lands. Four small dots hover around the text box, about 4% outside it, and spread to the new corners over about 5-8 frames after each word (F15-F18, F23-F25). At F54-F59 the gap between the two phrases opens by about 5% of frame width, then a hard cut at F60.
value.why: The eye has one target, the newest word, and the tint marks it for exactly as long as it takes to read it. The corner dots read as a selection box, saying 'this is being made' without a logo. The phrase split gives the cut a reason to happen.

value.name: card-collapses-to-underline
value.description: Hard cut at F60 to a photographic plate covered by a soft-edged black rounded card about 92% wide and 85% high. Over 12 frames (F60-F72) it shrinks toward a point near (0.45, 0.43), ease-out (frame difference 41, 33, 24, 16, 11, 6, 3, 1.7), flattening into a thin bar that becomes the white selection underline below the first icon of a floating dock; the icons fade in around it from F70.
value.why: The cut lands on darkness, not on the plate, so the change from white is a single dark block the eye can follow; it shrinks to exactly where the next point of interest, the selected icon, is. The viewer is handed from the line to the dock without a search.

value.name: mark-carry-iris-open
value.description: The mark detaches from its wordmark (F256), tumbles about a quarter turn while rising to x 0.5, y 0.2 and shrinking to about 4% of frame width (F256-F267, 11 frames); the wordmark slides out right, accelerating (F261-F266). After a 16-frame hold, a circle about 45% of frame width appears around the mark at F283 and opens to beyond the frame by F289 (6 frames, ease-out: difference 15, 21, 12.5, 8.7, 5.7, 3.8), revealing the product screen on a pastel ground, where the same mark is the screen's header at the same position.
value.why: The mark is the anchor across the boundary: the eye is already on it when the circle opens, so the new screen is read from its header downward. It also says, without words, that the brand and the interface are the same thing.

value.name: orbit-ring-flies-past-frame
value.description: A ring of about 30 rounded photo thumbnails, tilted in depth, orbits a centred line for 1.9 s. On exit the ring expands outward and off all four edges in 12 frames (F621-F633), accelerating (difference 13 to 37), so the centred line is left alone on white for one frame (F633); at F634 the line is replaced by the larger headline.
value.why: The line in the centre never moves, so the eye stays put while the periphery clears; clearing the frame by expansion rather than a cut makes the headline feel like it was inside the ring all along.

value.name: roll-exit-to-spinning-mark
value.description: The held headline block (with its chips) begins a clockwise roll and slight scale-up at F724, accelerating to about 12 degrees and 110% by F735 (11 frames, ease-in: difference 0.2 to 16.5). Hard cut at F736 to the mark at about 27% of frame height, still rotated about 20 degrees clockwise, which unrotates and shrinks with an ease-out over about 1.5 s to a square mark about 7% of frame width.
value.why: The rotation continues across the cut, so the eye reads one spin rather than two shots; the headline seems to turn into the brand. The fast in and slow settle give the end card weight.
